messages.text: Marco found that old photo of Dad standing by the tiny oak. Was that the first spring after you two moved in?
Close. The tree went in the year after, when the back lot was still mostly weeds and the garden was only four tomato cages.
That yard looks bigger every time I see the old pictures. No wonder Kathy gets nervous about keeping it all up.
She can worry. The oak is staying, and so am I.
Can you keep my spare key handy this weekend? Dave's conference got moved earlier. Cooper's food bin is full and his blue leash is by the mudroom.
Yes. I still have the key in the kitchen drawer. I'll bring him over after breakfast Saturday if that's easiest.
ty. And close your sewing-room door first unless you want Winston supervising from the wooden frame again.
Too late for that. He slept on Harold's pillow and is already graying up the quilt squares.
Found that lakeshore brochure in my glove box from when Dave and I went north. Did you ever take the boat tour with the cliffs?
Yes, Harold packed sandwiches and kept every receipt in the blue folder. Pretty water, too many stairs.
That sounds like him. ty for the folder idea, actually. Dave keeps saying just put it on the card and I keep hearing your voice.
We always liked coming home with the folder empty and the bank book still sensible.
Pat says she is bringing the score pads today. I hope she remembers how to count the left bower this time...
Harold would have enjoyed that. He always said I learned that table before I learned long division.
Also, Ray asked whether you might sit with him at fellowship next Sunday. I said I would let you answer for yourself.
Kind of you. I will sit with our usual group and deal him in if we are short a fourth.
The library sale has a DVD with Monument Valley on the cover, plus a little book of Brandywine barn pictures. Shall I set them aside until bridge?
Yes, please. The dusty red rocks and those plain Pennsylvania fields are exactly the sort of thing I like to look at while I mend.
There is also a scratched disc with old mountain harmonies. Track 3 is Wildwood Flower, if that means anything to you.
It does. If it plays through without skipping, bring that too.
Pat wants to move bridge supper to 6:30 next Tuesday... I told her you would prefer Mac's at 4:30 if we are taking your car.
4:30 is better. The CR-V is fine for downtown while it is still light.
That makes sense. I will tell Pat no scenic route and no lingering over dessert.
Thank you. I still have the cleanest windshield in Saline after those 2022 eye appointments, but glare is glare.
I can come from Ann Arbor after book club Thursday and help sort the birthday cards.
Thank you. I have Brian and Keisha's Denver envelope on the kitchen table already.
Good. Emma texted me that her Grand Valley clinical schedule changed again, so do not seal hers yet.
I will wait. I also found the lace tablecloth Sophie asked about, folded in the cedar chest.
Foggy but not slick. Still good for 8?
Yes. I will meet you behind the library, same bench.
Perfect. Let's keep it to the two today. I have a 9:30 call.
Two is plenty. I will bring the small thermos.
Did the Zoom behave this morning? I know you were worried about the sound again.
It behaved. Linda could hear me, and I found the little $40 nuisance before the others logged on.
Of course you did. That is exactly how they got you to keep doing those monthly pages in the first place.
It was only two numbers turned around. Same sort of thing Harold used to leave for me in a cigar box with carburetor slips.
Dr. Nguyen's office posted the new handout in the portal. I can print it Sunday if you would rather not read it on the tablet.
Thank you. I will look after the 6 o'clock program. The tablet behaves better if I do one thing at a time.
That is fine. I also checked CDC.gov, and it matches what his office sent. No need to chase the television ads.
Good. I trust your reading more than those loud commercials.
The forecast says sleet overnight. If the roads are slick in the morning, I can come up after 10 and carry the bags in.
I will see how it looks before I leave. I only need the usual things and I have $82 left in the March food envelope.
Please do not rush yourself. Busch's will still have your apples if you go a little later.
Nine is quiet there, and I like being home before the lunch crowd starts.
Library path looks shiny in patches. Still want 8, or porch coffee?
Let's do one loop only. I put the black stick in the car and Rob already scraped the driveway edge.
Good. I'll bring water and keep Cooper's leash out of your way. ty
I printed the pre-visit form. For the line asking weekly glasses, do you want me to put 0 unless it is a holiday week?
Yes. Put 0 for a regular week. The bathroom scale said 140.6 this morning before breakfast.
Got it. I will write 141 so they do not fuss over decimals. Did you find the old blue card with the height mark?
In the drawer with the thermometer. I will bring it Sunday.
Marco found the scanner setting I mentioned. If you send Richard the pages, set it to PDF, not photo.
I am doing each page one at a time. I have the bank screen on the laptop and the spiral open next to it.
That sounds like you. Please do not spend the whole afternoon making page 3 perfect.
Page 3 had two numbers that looked too close. I checked them twice more before I scanned it.
Mom, I found a book of postcard stamps in your blue desk drawer. Do you want me to bring it Sunday?
I picked up carrots and a small salad for tomorrow. I will be up at noon.
Yes, please. I used the last two this morning, one for Dolores and one for Ava's envelope.
Good. I have the crust chilling and the chicken cooked already.
Perfect. I need to leave by about 3:00, but we should still have time for the big puzzle page.
I will put them in my purse now. Also, Linda said the 9 o'clock check-in went smoothly yesterday.
I saved it. I only filled in the little one this morning.
Good. We only did the Adrian names and then she was ready to hang up.
I found two more reimbursement slips in my choir folder. They are from February, naturally...
Bring them Tuesday and I will tuck them behind the 3/3 deposit page. That makes 31 lines for the month, if I counted right.
Also, Linda said the committee wants to give you a little envelope this year. I told her to ask you first.
Please tell Linda no envelope. I can keep the columns straight because I want to, and I would rather leave it at that.
Leaving Toledo in about ten. I have the cranberry bread and Lily's photos.
Good. I put the porch mat down and cleared the blue room chair so you can stack anything for Emma.
Perfect. I found her charger in our hall closet, so I'll bring that up too. See you after 10.
Drive carefully. I have soup ready, no hurry.
We are leaving Toledo closer to ten. Greg asked if the Lions mug is still in the cupboard, and I told him yes, provided he behaves at lunch. 🙂
The mug is there. I have the same rule as 2016: turkey, children, weather, and no lecturing across my table.
Understood. I will remind him. Also Daniel texted me that he and Marco may call tomorrow if the dahlias survived the cold snap.
Seven my time is already written down. If Daniel carries the phone too fast through those raised beds, I get dizzy.
I can stop at Meijer before I come up. Do you still want me to keep you around $85 for the week, or is March different?
If you can keep it under $90, that keeps the month near my 350 line.
Got it. Also, the pharmacy bag on your counter had an $88 receipt clipped to it. Was that already in your checkbook?
Yes, I put it with the 185 and 125 papers so Kathy can see the whole stack Sunday.
I found a skein of that soft green you liked at the Toledo craft store. Want me to bring it up next month?
Yes, thank you. The blue is getting low and I have been saving the last bit for the chair after supper.
I will put it with the kids' things. Also Sophie said the book with the 1918 nurse is good but sad.
That one is on my side table. I may do a few rows first so I do not read too late.
Still good for 7 your time? I can show you the fig buds before it gets too dark here.
Yes. I have washed my dinner plate and put it back in the hutch. I will be settled by then.
Still good for 7? I can show you where the fig buds finally opened.
Still good for 7 your time? I can show you the fig buds before the light goes.
Yes. Kathy has just gone and I am putting the pie plate to soak.
Yes. I finished my supper dishes and did my evening mail sweep, and your garden note was sitting in Primary.
You and that hutch. Marco says hello and wants to know whether you beat the Sunday puzzle.
Nearly. I started it with coffee before the oatmeal got cold.
Perfect. Just tap the little camera by my name if my call does not pop up.
Tell me you two did not leave half the clues blank again.
Only the corner with all the opera names. I had the small one done before breakfast.
The phone is on the charger by Harold's chair. I will answer when it sings at me.
Portland is finally getting a dry evening, so I will walk you past the fig tree on video in a minute.
Marco says the thyme in your Sunday pan is still better than anything I buy out here. Did you use the last of the porch bundle?
Good. I want to hear whether Jacob's spring break starts before your dahlias go in.
Before I forget: did the Vanguard 1099 finally come in, or is it still hiding in the mail pile?
Not the last. I trimmed it before church and tucked some rosemary in too. Kathy took two helpings, so that is answer enough.
It came Thursday. I put it behind the Bank of Ann Arbor money market page. That page says $42,0-something, close enough for Kathy's tax folder.
It starts Friday. He is mostly thinking about track and whether Marco will make pancakes.
I will show you the fig buds on video in a bit. Send me a picture of the tomato starts if they have done anything.
Good. And the Visa sweep still happens on the 12th? I just want the spreadsheet to match your statement.
They are under the laundry-room light. Cabbage tray looks stronger than the tomatoes this week.
Yes, the whole thing goes out on the 12th. I waited to buy quilt backing until after I put back the last bit from that furnace motor bill.
Ask him to send a picture. Also tell me if Rebecca has heard anything more about Sophie and Nate's June idea.
Good morning. I am leaving after church and can stop at Walgreens if the March bottle is ready.
Thank you, but I still have enough of the 20 mg tablets until Thursday. I did the 7:15 row already.
All right. Please set the D and calcium back in the tray before you forget. I will bring salad at noon.
They are back beside the multi and the little 81. See you at noon.
I can take you for the May pictures. Did Dr. Nguyen's office send the order yet, or should I call IHA Saline on Monday?
Please do not call yet. The portal says pending, and they usually push it through after the March paperwork.
All right. Also bring the blue card Sunday so I can make a clean copy for your file. The 2023 line is getting hard to read.
It is in the kitchen drawer with the old 2005 folder. I will put both on the table.
Before I come at noon, do you want me to look over that health history sheet? They always want dates for anything new since last spring.
Yes please. I have the March 19 note from the office on Eisenhower, and the November pharmacy slips are clipped together.
Tom's oven is running behind. Could I come at 12:30 instead of noon with the salad?
Yes. I had written noon on the pad, so I am moving the potatoes to 12:10 and leaving the table alone until then.
Good. I remember the November one because you were on the couch with tea for nearly a week, then much better after the second bottle was started.
And the March one was only that small thing on my back. They mailed the all-clear page afterward.
That sounds fine. Please do your 3:00 cup in the sunroom before we touch any more boxes from Dad's workshop.
I will. I don't want another day like those February mornings when the curtains stayed shut.
I am leaving in ten minutes. Do you want me to bring the suet cakes from Tractor Supply, or did you already get them?
Bring two if you do not mind. I used the last one this morning and then sat out back with my coffee and the small notebook.
Of course. I will also bring a fresh brush for the tray. You said the old one was getting grimy.
Thank you. I do not like leaving that mess where the squirrels and the little visitors eat.
Mom, I found the old navy folder in the cedar chest when I moved the quilts. Do you still want the St. Agnes report card page?
Yes, please bring it next first Saturday. The lady at WCC said older records sometimes help if the course names changed.
Okay. There is also a note in very neat handwriting saying you were 'quick with columns.' I will tuck that in too. 🙂
That would be Sister Mary Agnes. She had firmer plans for me than I had for myself in 1960.
I saved that Food Network lemon cake recipe but I know you usually just do your little square of dark chocolate now. Want me to bring berries instead when I come up?
Berries would be lovely. I have my oatmeal and coffee covered for morning, and I will make chicken soup for lunch.
Perfect. Greg can have the cake at home. You have been steady about passing on that sort of thing since 2012.
It is easier if I do not start. A square after supper is plenty.
That pot pie photo looked serious. Did you make both pans yesterday or was one from the freezer?
Both pans were fresh. One stayed here for supper, and one is wrapped tight with a strip of masking tape on the lid.
Good system. Marco says label the date too or you will end up guessing in April.
I wrote March 9 and 'no mushrooms.' Sarah remembered that from the last Sunday table.
When we FaceTime Sunday, can we look at the house tab you made in January? I can help add the July and December county lines if you want.
That would help. I already penciled in 2,400 for an ordinary month, but the county lines make the page look lopsided.
That is exactly what tabs are for. We can keep the one-time items from making the regular weeks look strange. Love you.
Love you too. I will have the laptop open after supper.
I just saw tomorrow's forecast. Wet and windy... I can pick you up at 12:35 if you would rather not drive.
Thank you. I put the little beige case by my purse so I do not forget it this time.
Good. Also, if Pat opens with the school board mess again, I am dealing the first hand immediately.
Deal fast. We can save the article you sent for after coffee.
Still walking at 8? Path behind library should be dry. Also I saw your porch flag is back up.
Yes. I put it out after breakfast. The old D one can stay until the men come north.
ty. I will bring the water. Did the Crisler ladies make you holler last night?
Only once, and Cooper would not have liked the noise. That last rebound was worth it.
Are you still coming for bridge at one? Pat says she can park close to the east door if that helps.
Yes. I did my two tablets with breakfast, so the knees should behave well enough for cards.
Good. I made ginger tea this morning and thought of you. My cousin keeps pushing bottles from that little shop downtown... I am ignoring him.
Wise. With the blood pressure pill I leave mystery bottles alone. Tea and the warm pad are enough for me.
Did the knees forgive you after Saturday? You said the Maple sidewalk was clear enough to go over on foot.
Mostly. I was glad I only stayed for the 10 to noon part with the little ones this time.
Two hours of small chairs sounds plenty... Save the heroic version for someone under seventy.
Exactly. I still had enough legs left to cut through by Mill Pond before lunch.
City letter says the Michigan Ave sidewalk flags by your drive are on the list. I can look after work if you want.
Thank you. It is the old section doing what old sections do.
Your back stretch is the one I'd worry about more. That's a lot of grass after rain.
I know every low spot in that third of an acre. Harold's oak takes the wet corner like a champ.
Marco found the courthouse picture from 2015 while looking for tax papers. We both laughed at my terrible tie.
Send it Sunday before you start roaming the yard with the phone. I want to compare it with the old Detroit picture of you and your dad.
Deal. Also, we mailed checks this morning, so if Greg starts in about 'where money goes,' I am stepping away from the screen.
That is why the old dinner rule stays. Kathy can argue all day, Rebecca goes quiet, and I still have to wash the plates.
Did Kathy get your March numbers into the spreadsheet? I can make the Portland column disappear if it is cluttering your view.
I still laugh thinking about Dad's shoebox system. Did you ever find the year he put everything in envelopes by mower brand?
She did. The big ones are 800 for the house tax account, 220 lights and water, 120 house policy, and 85 car policy.
1987 and 1988. Briggs in one stack, Tecumseh in another, 1099 slips paper-clipped to the back. The best year was just shy of $3,000.
That explains why your totals always balanced when mine never did.
That is clear. Where did you put the three medical-card drafts?
It also explains why Linda's QBO export bothers me when a deposit is posted to the wrong month.
Same sheet, below the car gas line. They come to 398 this month unless the pharmacy changes.
Route behind the library is clear. Bring water and maybe your little reader if you want to check it before coffee. ty
I will. I already had oatmeal with berries, so I should be fine for two miles.
Good. I packed almonds, not muffins. See you at 8.
Thank you. Almonds are safer than muffins for me in the morning.
Route by the library still icy. Want to push walk to 8:15?
That is fine. I have finished my oatmeal and the puzzle corner. I will bring the small water bottle.
ty. Cooper tried to steal one mitten, so we are all starting slowly.
Library path is icy by the curb. Want the shorter loop and coffee after? I have the low porch chair out.
I will be at the library doors. I need to be home in time to lay out supper before the afternoon gets away from me.
Shorter loop is sensible. I measured 63 on Kathy's wall chart, so the chair is easier than the tall one lately.
np. I also saved you one of Dave's tiny cordial glasses from Saturday. It looked more your speed than the big stemware.
That is plenty for me. I mostly just like the toast.
Walk route still muddy by the library. Want me to swing by after and help move that big print away from the window?
That would help. The girl in the pale dress is fading where the morning sun hits her.
np. Also Dave found a channel running those old Wayne-in-the-desert movies Saturday night.
Thank him for me. I will put my sewing basket by the chair and let the guitar music wait until Sunday.
Good walk. ty for slowing down by the library steps.
My knees were grateful. I will be quiet tonight with the lamp and that pile by my chair.
The one with the old London map on the cover?
Yes. If I behave, two chapters and six inches on the sleeve before bed.
I can wash the blue-room sheets when I come Sunday, unless Rebecca already started them after lunch.
She stripped the bed but left the hamper by the sewing table.
That works. Emma texted me that her May dates may be May 10 through 17, depending on her last exam.
Tell her I will keep the small desk clear. She likes that corner by the window.
I put the lint roller and the vet folder on your hall table. The 2020 Humane Society papers were mixed in with Harold's old receipts.
Thank you. Winston is pretending the folder belongs under him.
Of course he is. Eleanor waved when I left and said Cooper behaved for you Saturday.
He did, though he tried to take me down Henry Street faster than my knees wanted.
Rob left the receipt on the porch rail. He wrote $40 for Tuesday morning.
I saw it. Worth every penny after that January business. I can still do my own grass when the season starts.
I know you can. Please have the mower shop check the self-propel before you wrestle it around the maple roots.
Already on my list. The wheeled contraption you suggested is staying in the basement.
Did you and Eleanor get rained on this morning, or did the clouds behave?
They behaved until we reached the library doors again. We did not try for the old three.
Wise. Knees have a way of making their opinions known...
Mine were clear enough before breakfast.
Pat just called. She cannot make bridge Tuesday, so Ruth suggested Thursday instead... naturally.
I saved you the church address sheet. Dolores Klein is still at the same Tecumseh Road address, it says.
Thank you. I am updating my December list early while I have the good pen out.
Thursday is not where Tuesday belongs, but I am trying to bend a little. Harold would be shaking his head at my pencil marks.
Ken would say the same about my calendar. Shall I pick you up after your sunroom cup, say 3:20?
Very sensible. Did you reach Maggie before bridge, or is that the Friday morning one?
3:20 works. That gives me the quiet ten minutes first, which helps more than I expected.
Friday at 9. I clipped the Adrian page so I do not spend the whole time hunting for it.
Did the WCC person ever call back about the two classes you circled? I can make the PDF bigger if the catalog print is too tiny.
Mom, I found a native seed mix that should do well along your back fence. Want me to mail a packet, or would that just become another Daniel project?
She did. BUS 121 is evenings, and ACC 122 has a Tuesday morning seat if I can manage parking.
Mail it. That strip is bare, and I would rather fill it with something useful than have the lawn company fuss with it.
Tuesday sounds more humane. And for what it's worth, the nun who spotted your ledger brain would be pleased.
Good. Leave the old stems a little longer if you can stand the untidiness. They help more than they look like they do.
She told me that before your father bought the ring. I remember the exact hallway.
I can stand it. The back window has been busy enough this week that I do not want to disturb the corner.
Route behind the library is icy. Want to skip today and do Monday? No sense repeating last November's couch week.
Monday is better. I still have the note where Dr. Shah said no cold air until the last pills were finished.
Good call. Also if you are sorting records, keep that little back-site letter with your regular papers. Clinics lose things.
Already in the blue folder, right behind the March bill.
I can pick up the copy paper before Sunday lunch. Do you still need the narrow receipt tape for your church folder?
Yes, please. The old calculator is fussy but it prints cleanly, and I still like a paper trail.
Mom, when they ask about reimbursing your supplies, please let them at least cover the paper.
Paper is different. My time is mine to give. I will save the receipt for Staples.
Did they have decent pears this morning, or has March defeated even Busch's produce aisle?
Pears were hard as rocks. I stayed with oranges and oatmeal. Total was $76.43, so March is still behaving.
That is restraint. I will wait for the Saturday tables downtown, when the berries stop costing more than jewelry.
I put a little cash aside for those weeks. It is easier if I plan it before June starts.
Mom, Lily found two board books in my trunk. Are those yours or did I steal from the Maple Rd pile? :)
Mine, I think. Put them by your purse and I will take them over tomorrow morning.
Do you want me to swing them up before I go to Toledo, or are you walking?
Forecast says dry, so I will go on my own. It is only the morning stretch now, not the old long one.
Marco found an old deck in the kitchen drawer and asked why you always say never lead trump unless you mean it.
Because the Cintron children were raised properly. Your father heard me say that the very first evening he took me out.
I can hear Dad laughing at that. Did the church fellow ever quit asking you to go somewhere after service?
Yes. I was polite, and I was plain. Fellowship coffee is enough.
I found the Paducah brochure you mentioned tucked inside my Great Lakes folder... no idea why it was there.
Save it for me, please. I want to compare the exhibits with that Missouri Star stop in Hamilton if my hands cooperate.
I will bring it Tuesday. Perhaps we should plan the route before Pat starts another bridge argument.
Good. I only worked 80 minutes this morning, so I still have enough grip left to hold cards.
The WTVS segment at six was clearer than the newspaper piece, I thought... especially the last two minutes.
I wrote down the name so I can compare it with Consumer Reports tomorrow after church.
Good plan. I am setting the coffee pot early for Meet the Press. Face the Nation if my patience holds.
I will have mine on too, though I may need a second cup by the panel.
Mom, did Sophie's dress photo come through? I sent it with the link last night.
I saw the picture in our blue-message thread first, then found the store note in Promotions with my coffee.
Good. If Lily is home later, she wants to wave from my kitchen for two minutes. Around 7:15?
That is fine. I will do my evening inbox after supper and keep the phone beside me.
I bought tomato seedlings too early, didn't I? They look leggy already. 🙂
Put them in the brightest window and turn the pot each morning. Once May settles, I fuss with mine from 7 to 8 before the phone starts.
Can I bring you apples on the next first Saturday? The farm stand near us had a nice bag.
Yes, if they are firm ones. I have the square pan ready, and carrots from the cold bin can go into the noon meal.
Mom, Greg asked if your Honda is still the same one from the dealer by the mall. He is looking at used SUVs again.
Same 2019 CR-V. I kept the folder because Harold was so pleased we did it without a monthly bill.
That sounds like Dad. We can talk numbers when I come up, but I will make sure we leave Toledo early enough.
Early is best. I would rather be home before the headlights start bothering my eyes.
Mom, Greg found a cheap Charleston package ad. Made me think of your photo with the iron gate and the pink jacket. Was that the same trip with the little inn?
Same one. We stayed two nights and ate shrimp on East Bay Street. Harold had the amount written on an index card before we left Saline.
Of course he did :) Greg would faint at an index card.
It kept us from arguing at the desk when we checked out.
I will be up at noon with salad. Do you want me to look at the furnace paperwork while I am there?
Yes, please. The November motor receipt is in the drawer, $380. I wrote Feb and March beside it so I would remember I made it whole again.
That sounds organized. Please also leave out the house tax notice and the car insurance card so I can copy them for your folder.
They are by the Chase CD slips. No house payment booklet to hunt for, at least.
Lily says your bracket sheet has more notes than her chemistry lab. 🙂
Tell her I only marked the women who know how to box out. The Ann Arbor line is underlined twice.
Do you want me to look for that navy cap with the white D when we come up? Greg found a bin of old hats.
Yes, please. The brim on mine is tired, and April looks better with that cap by the kitchen radio.
Before I forget, how was the walk today? You sounded better after last Thursday's shorter loop.
Two miles is the right amount now. Right hip grumbled on the hill, but it settled once I came home and used the warm pad.
Good. And thank you for not taking cousin Tommy's 2020 gummy suggestion as medical advice. Marco still laughs about how fast you changed the subject.
I remember. I told him I had my drugstore tablets and a sidewalk, and that was plenty.
Wind is mean this morning. Want to shorten the walk and do coffee after? ty
Yes, two miles is plenty. I am hoping March comes in nearer 1,900 now that the furnace is not running all day.
Same here. Dave said our gas drops hard once April settles in. Bring the blue jacket.
Still walking at 8? I may cut it short. Work wants me early.
Yes, two miles is fine. I need to be back before IHA calls about the May slot.
Got it. Bring your water. Also if they ask dates, I can help read the card after the walk - you showed me the 2021 pair last year.
Thank you. The spring 2021 lines are clear, it is the fall one that smudged.
Did you get back to sleep after you called Marjorie? I saw your kitchen light when Tom let Winston out.
A little. She answered on the second ring and talked me down while the wind was rattling the porch door.
I am glad it was her. Please put the left earpiece in before cards today if you are still tired.
It is in the charger now. I will let Marjorie drive if the gusts keep up.
Do you still want me to phone Ruth about the 22nd? She said she can bring napkins if we are short.
Yes, please. I have eleven marked yes and one maybe, so twelve places should do it.
I will tell her. Sarah also asked whether you meant the front kettle or the little blue one for their stop afterward.
The blue one. I will pull the labeled pan from the freezer Saturday night so it is not solid as a brick.
Still walking at 8? cold but dry.
Yes. I need to stretch my fingers anyway after last night's red border.
Bring the little hook thing if you want. I can drop you at church after.
Route behind library is clear. Want me to bring water?
Yes please. I am just finishing the 7:15 things and putting the little bottles back.
Thank you. Fourth Thursday group starts at 6:30 tonight, but I may only stay till 8.
np. Same two-mile loop, no hill today.
Good. Kathy reminded me not to leave the 20 mg one next to the calcium again.
I found the folder you asked about. The bank letter is clipped to Rebecca's graduation invitation, just like you said.
Good. Your father saved everything neatly that year.
Also, after seeing the gutter estimate, I am going to say my monthly practical sentence: a smaller place would mean fewer of these lists.
Sentence received. Sunday we can talk gutters, not packing.
Are you still coming to Mac's tomorrow, or did the March paperwork win?
I can come. I only have to copy the water bill confirmation into the spiral and find the old Beauchamp envelope.
Of course there is an old envelope. You would not trust a stack unless every corner lined up.
The corners help me catch what is missing.
For bridge Tuesday, Pat is threatening brownies again... I can bring cheese and apple slices instead.
Cheese and apples would be better. I will eat my salad with chicken before I come, so I do not pick at everything.
Very sensible. Did Kathy get the Medicare paperwork settled for that arm patch, or is it still a nuisance?
Settled, thank goodness. It is covered this round, and I only need to stop by Walgreens after cards.
Toledo traffic was awful today, so I may leave earlier when I come up next time. Caleb needs to be back at BG by dinner.
That is fine. Bring Lily's schedule if she wants me to put the meets on my calendar.
I will. Sophie is asking whether you still have Grandpa's small address book for the invitation list.
It is in the desk drawer with the old stamps. I will set it out.
Marco put on that album you like while I was staking the dahlias. The autoharp part is prettier than I remembered.
That bright strum is the best part. It sounds like a kitchen table with everyone singing close together.
I also found a Portland shop with a postcard of a weathered farmhouse in dry grass. It reminded me of the print over your desk.
Save it for July if you can. I will trade you the movie with the long doorway shot Harold always liked.
Traverse City dates are firm now: May 18-22. Can Cooper stay with your routine again or should I ask the college kid on Maple?
Put me down. I can do mornings and supper, same as last time.
np, ty. I'll return the favor if you need me after Winston's checkup. Is he still around 16?
About that, unless he has been eating quilt batting. He'll be offended by the scale either way.
Lily asked what you are making when Aunt Kathy comes tomorrow. She remembers the gravy from last time. :)
Chicken pot pie this time. Kathy said she can stay until 3 if I do not make her take leftovers.
That sounds like her. Did you save the paper insert for the two of you?
Yes, and I finished today's little grid with my coffee.
Marco found a box of old postcards at Powell's today. One was Mackinac with the Grand Hotel porch, and I immediately pictured Dad counting out the ferry money.
He would have had it clipped inside the AAA book. We bought fudge after he checked what was left.
That tracks. Did you two do that before or after the painted cliffs up north?
Before, I think. The cliffs were the year your father bought the green cooler.
Marco says to ask whether you want us to rent a car in July or just use yours for errands.
You can use mine. The Honda is easy to park, and it is paid for, so I am not precious about the mileage.
Good. We will handle any evening grocery runs, then. No need for you to be out with all those bright lanes on Michigan Ave.
That would help. Daytime Meijer is plenty.
Caleb says you still owe him a lesson on the game with bowers when he comes up in April. He only remembers you beating Grandpa at the lake.
I will teach him, but he has to learn the farmers' hand properly. Grandpa was a good loser most of the time.
Mom, Mrs. Keller from church told me Ray was asking after you again. Do you want me to say anything if she brings it up?
No need. I answered him once, kindly. I am content with family, church, and my card table.
I put the Detroit envelope back in the cedar chest after lunch. The one with Dad's Tigers cap is on top, just as Daniel asked.
Thank you. He and Marco liked seeing it last night, though Daniel nearly dropped the phone turning toward the blueberry bushes.
That sounds like him. Also, Rebecca called me about Thanksgiving seating already. I said I would sit by Greg if you want the quiet end protected.
We will keep the 2016 rule and place the pies between the loud ones.
Rain looks ugly. Want to skip the library loop today?
Yes, thank you. I need the extra time anyway. Three envelopes to finish before my 9 o'clock call.
np. I can drop those at the blue box when I take Cooper out.
That would help. One is for Dolores, and the small pink one is for Lily.
Are you still coming early before bridge, or did Linda keep you in the front office again...
Coming early. I left her the March board packet and circled one grant receipt that QBO put in the wrong column.
Good. We need you at the card table, not chasing forty dollars down a hallway.
That old forty dollars bought me four years of Tuesday interruptions, apparently.
I found my receipt file at last. Mine is not as neat as yours... did you finish your March envelope arithmetic?
Almost. The three health envelopes were 185, 125, and 88. I rounded the grocery line to 350 and the church check to 200.
That is a tidy way to do it. I may copy you, though not with quite so many clips and rubber bands.
The clips keep me from paying the wrong thing twice.
Ruth says we are one point apart after today. Pat would have noticed if she had not spent the second rubber muttering about yard signs.
I heard enough of that from my good ear. Thank you for changing the subject to the scout jamboree story.
Those boys and their lopsided pinewood cars... 1972 feels like last Tuesday sometimes.
And somehow we are still packing snacks for Tuesdays.
Mom, I found that little envelope you gave me last year in my glove box. Do you still need the March 2025 paperwork from the Ann Arbor office?
Yes, if it has the page saying there was nothing to do after they took it off my back.
It does. I can bring it April 4. Do you also want me to print the Walgreens list from when you sounded awful after Thanksgiving?
Please. The two medicines were only for ten days, but the form asks for anything since last year.
No need to call tonight if you are settled in. Marco says he is impressed by anyone who can count stitches and follow a Tudor court plot at the same time.
Tell Marco I cannot do both at once. The book waits while I fix the cuff.
Fair. Send a picture when the cuff behaves. I will send dahlias tomorrow. ❤️
I will. It is just me and the floor lamp this evening.
Dave says the rear lot is full of cones. Want me to cross over at 7:50 and we can drive one car?
That would help. Funny to think you have been crossing that street for me since the apple butter year.
2014 and still worth it. We'll park by the book drop and do the two.
I will be ready with my jacket.
ty for the heads up about the plastic netting by the library path. I grabbed it after our walk.
Good. I thought about it all the way home. Those little feet get caught in things like that.
Also saw your binoculars on the porch rail when I came back with Cooper. Did your speckled visitor show?
Only for a moment, but I wrote it down. Cooper was very polite and did not bark at the tray.
Dr. Nguyen's nurse called me back. She said your May 14 appointment is fine and the order will go to St. Joe's by the first week of April.
Good. That gives me time to find the films they always ask about from before everything went digital.
She also said your chart shows the October entry, the pneumonia one, both shingles dates, Tdap, and the four newer-virus dates through 2023.
Then I will stop carrying three copies in my purse. Maybe two.
The forecast says the church lot may be crusty tomorrow morning... shall I pull up by the side door?
That would be kind. I will bring the black-handled stick, just for the lot. Rob is coming before breakfast if the driveway needs it.
Good. No heroics before bridge season resumes in earnest.
No heroics. But when April comes I am still mowing my own front strip.
Do you want me to bring anything when I come up next weekend? I can stop before I leave Toledo. 🙂
No, thank you. I will do my Busch's list in the morning and keep it light. I am trying to land March near $350.
That sounds like you. Are you still saving a little for those downtown Saturday peaches once the tents come back?
Yes. Those are worth planning for, especially in July.
I printed the travel checklist for July. Do you want me to add the morning row to it?
Yes. Put 7:15 on there, please, and write 20 mg plus multi, D, calcium, and 81 so I do not pack twice.
Done. I also left a blank line for the pharmacy phone number in case Kathy has the current one.
Good thinking. That same bottle has followed me since the late nineties, so I do not like improvising.
Maple is clear this morning. I passed the pond path with Cooper. Bit windy but dry.
Good. I need that report for tomorrow before I decide on shoes.
For the 10 thing at the children's desk? I can drop you if the wind gets worse. np
Route behind the library is muddy. Want to switch to the sidewalk loop Monday? ty
Sidewalk loop is fine. I will be done out back by 8 if I start at 7.
Thank you, but I should manage. Four blocks to the pond and then the rest on Maple is fine when it is dry.
Need any jars from the hardware store? I'm going after work.
Only regular lids if they have them. The cabbage row gets ahead of me every year, and I dislike finding that out too late.
Good morning. I sent the appointment form again, in case the first one landed somewhere odd.
It was in Updates when I checked after breakfast. I starred it so I will not lose it.
Thank you. Text me if the attachment will not open, and we can do the little camera call after supper.
I can open it. I will look once more tonight before I set the phone on the bedroom charger.
I can come up after lunch Sunday and help you sort the papers from DTE and the county envelope. Please do not leave them on the stairs.
They are on the dining room table. February finished at 3,200, but March should sit closer to my regular 2,400 once I enter the last grocery receipt.
Good. I will bring salad and we can check the January file after the crossword.
I can take you to campus on Monday if you decide to sign the audit form. I will bring the magnifier for the course sheet.
That sounds fine. I still need to put Rebecca's family birthdays on the right row.
Thank you. I keep thinking it is foolish at my age, and then I see Sister Mary Agnes's note and get stubborn.
It is not foolish. You have balanced church ledgers for forty years. Two more classes and a parking pass are not going to scare you.
Your father used to say I could make a column of numbers behave better than any of us children.
I can bring quart bags Sunday after lunch if you are low. I saw only two left in your drawer.
Please do. I used the last good ones on the beef stew containers after Jim and Sarah left.
All right. Are you still setting the long table again on April 12, or is someone else doing it?
I will do it. Twelve still fits if I borrow the two folding chairs from the coat room.
At bridge Tuesday, remind me to ask how the out-of-town cards turned out... Denver, Portland, Toledo, all those stamps.
I used five stamps before I found the right Grand Valley address for Emma.
Better than my method, which is to put things in a pile and hope the post office understands me.
Sophie called after supper too. She and Nate are still deciding between a church hall and his aunt's garden.
Sarah says the April luncheon forms are already coming in. She sounded mildly afraid of the shoebox.
Tell Sarah the shoebox is harmless if people write their names legibly. I will sort checks from cash before bridge if she drops it on my porch.
She also mentioned putting you on the spring appreciation list with a gift card.
A thank-you at lunch is plenty. If there is a gift card, use it for coffee supplies in the kitchen.
I forgot to ask whether Ruth returned your serving spoon after cards... she left in such a hurry.
She did. It is back in the drawer under the good plates. I had the table cleared before the news started.
Of course you did. I am still looking at my bridge napkins from Tuesday.
Leave them for morning. I am putting my pencil by the crossword and going upstairs soon.
Mom, do you want me to bring that roll-on Caleb got from his coach when I come next Saturday? He swears by it after games. :)
No thank you, honey. I am keeping it simple: my two Tylenol when I need them, walking with Ellen, tea, and the heating pad.
Fair. I remember you shutting Tommy down in 2020 too. I will bring the lemon cake instead.
Mom, do you still want me to stop at Joann's before the April visit? They have batting on sale.
Lemon cake is much safer for my pill case.
Not this month, honey. I pinched that line for January and February after the furnace man, and I am just getting back to my usual rhythm.
Okay. I can bring the coupons anyway. Did the car registration renewal come through all right?
Yes, just the plate fee and insurance card. I paid Visa this morning and tucked the receipt with the Bank of Ann Arbor statement.
Mom, the Ypsi Facebook group approved your post. Someone already commented with hotel advice for western Kentucky. :)
I saw that. I asked about the big museum hours and whether Hamilton is worth the extra stop for fabric.
Your cart from Missouri Star is still open on my laptop from when I helped you. Do you want the red backing or should I close it?
Leave it. I want to match it to the little cream square tomorrow before my hands give out.
Do you want me to bring stamps tomorrow? I am stopping at Kroger before I drive up.
Yes, please. The envelope to Richard is ready except I want to look at the online payment list against my notebook one last time.
Okay. I will grab a book too so you can take your time. 🙂
It will not take long. I just want the $250 check and the copies in the same order as the folder.
For Sophie's shower, should I get one bottle for the toast or just sparkling juice? I cannot remember what you actually use at parties. 🙂
One bottle is enough if others want it. I will take the smallest pour and then coffee.
Okay. Also, Lily is bringing the black dress for you to try. She said it may need the shoulder taken up now that the old 5-5 tag is nonsense.
Tell her pins are welcome. The doctor wrote 63 inches last week, so the tag gave us a laugh.
Before our call tomorrow, should I send you the box score from today or will that spoil your radio replay?
Do not spoil it. I saved the Free Press page and will listen after supper.
Fair. Marco also asks whether the Ann Arbor women survived the second half. He heard you clapped loud enough for Portland.
They made it harder than necessary, but I kept the maize towel out. I will tell you both tomorrow.
Pat wants to borrow your cavalry trilogy after bridge Tuesday. I told her you would only lend the one with the envelope still inside the case.
Correct. The envelope has the museum postcard and the list of songs I wrote down from the end credits.
I will keep her honest... and I found your missing Sunny Side disc under the score pad.
Good. Bring it Tuesday, and I will send Pat home with the movie after I check the case.
April 4 still good for you? I can bring the grocery bags and the lamp Emma left at our place.
Yes. I will write it by the kitchen phone and clear the blue room dresser drawer.
She'll like that. She said the May week will feel short after Christmas, but she wants the quiet desk again.
I will have the little lamp waiting. Bring yourself, not too many errands.
Marco's flight is late. Can we do 7:20 your time instead of 7:00? I can still show you the fig tree buds.
All right. I wrote 7:20 over the old time and did not fuss with the whole evening, which I am counting as progress.
Good. How was today after the hard week around Dad's date?
Quieter. I kept the 3:00 tea, opened the back curtains, and went through only one envelope from his desk.
Walk tomorrow still ok? Also did you catch the Fauci clip this morning or should I send it?
I saw the first table round and then switched for the second one. Send it if it was on after that.

That is why I like him. I will read it after tonight's WTVS hour.
